hydrology.goal: Water of viscosity μ seeps through rock of permeability k, across an area A, driven by a pressure difference P over a length L. Write the flow Q.
hydrology.name: Darcy's law
hydrology.ask: Find Q in litres a second for k = 1e-11 m², A = 10 m², P = 1e5 Pa, m = 0.001 Pa·s (water), L = 10 m.
hydrology.method: Like current through a resistor: flow grows with the push (the pressure gradient) and the ease of passage (k/μ).

climatology.goal: The air's carbon dioxide rises from a concentration c to C. Write the radiative forcing F it adds, in W/m², which grows with the logarithm of the ratio (coefficient 5.35).
climatology.name: CO2 radiative forcing
climatology.ask: Find F for doubling the pre-industrial carbon dioxide: c = 280 ppm, C = 560 ppm.
climatology.method: The strongest absorption bands are already saturated; extra CO₂ only widens their wings, so each doubling adds the same.

remote_sensing.goal: A satellite at height h looks down through a telescope of aperture D at light of wavelength λ. Write the smallest separation x it can tell apart on the surface.
remote_sensing.name: Diffraction-limited footprint
remote_sensing.ask: Find x in metres for L = 5e-7 m, h = 7e5 m, D = 1.1 m.
remote_sensing.method: The smallest angle a circular aperture resolves is 1.22λ/D; at distance h that angle spans x.

planetary_geology.goal: A planet of mass M and radius R, of even density, squeezes its centre. Write the pressure P there, with gravity's constant G.
planetary_geology.name: Central pressure of a uniform planet
planetary_geology.ask: Find P in GPa (u = 1e9) for the Earth: M = 5.972e24 kg, R = 6.371e6 m, G = 6.674e-11.
planetary_geology.method: Integrate dP/dr = −ρg(r) from the surface in, with g(r) = (4/3)πGρr.

geodesics.goal: A mass M is squeezed until light cannot escape it. Write the radius r at which that happens, from gravity's constant G and the speed of light c.
geodesics.name: Schwarzschild radius
geodesics.ask: Find r in kilometres for the Sun: M = 1.989e30 kg, G = 6.674e-11, c = 2.998e8 m/s.
geodesics.method: Where the escape speed √(2GM/r) reaches c - which, by luck, is exactly what general relativity gives too.

gravitational_lensing.goal: A ray passes a mass M at closest distance b and is bent. Write the angle α it turns through, with G and c.
gravitational_lensing.name: Einstein deflection
gravitational_lensing.ask: Find α in arcseconds for starlight grazing the Sun: M = 1.989e30 kg, b = 6.96e8 m, G = 6.674e-11, c = 2.998e8 m/s.
gravitational_lensing.method: Newton gives 2GM/(c²b); curved space adds as much again - which Eddington's 1919 eclipse confirmed.

frame_dragging.goal: A body with angular momentum L drags the spacetime round it. Write the rate Ω at which a gyroscope's axis is turned at distance r, with G and c.
frame_dragging.name: Lense-Thirring precession
frame_dragging.ask: Find Ω in milliarcseconds a year (u = 6.51e15) above the Earth: L = 5.86e33 kg·m²/s, r = 7.02e6 m, G = 6.674e-11, c = 2.998e8.
frame_dragging.method: The spinning mass makes a gravitomagnetic field, a dipole like a spinning charge's; a gyroscope precesses in it.

tidal_physics.goal: A body of length L hangs head-down at distance r from a mass M. Write the difference a between the pull on its two ends, with G.
tidal_physics.name: Spaghettification
tidal_physics.ask: Find a in g for a 2 m body 100 km from a 10-solar-mass black hole: M = 1.989e31 kg, L = 2, r = 1e5, G = 6.674e-11.
tidal_physics.method: Differentiate GM/r² with respect to r and multiply by L.

binary_mergers.goal: Two masses m and n spiral together. Their gravitational waves depend on one combination of the two, which sets how fast the pitch rises. Write it, M.
binary_mergers.name: Chirp mass
binary_mergers.ask: Find M in solar masses for GW150914: m = 36, n = 29.
binary_mergers.method: The frequency rises as df/dt ∝ M^(5/3) f^(11/3) at leading order: only this combination enters.

alcubierre_metric.goal: Energy and mass are one: write the energy E locked in a mass M, with the speed of light c.
alcubierre_metric.name: Mass-energy equivalence
alcubierre_metric.ask: Find E in units of 10⁴⁴ J (u = 1e44) for the mass of Jupiter, M = 1.898e27 kg - roughly the negative energy a small warp bubble needs (c = 2.998e8 m/s).
alcubierre_metric.method: From the energy of a body at rest in special relativity: E² = (pc)² + (mc²)² with p = 0.
